assumptions.condition: The observed outcome for pair \((i,j)\) equals \(Y^{(W_{B,i},W_{S,j})}_{ij}\).

novel.justification: Persistent low-rank buyer--seller interaction is natural when a few marketplace segments or recommendation channels drive spillovers; additive schedules give \(\rho=0\), while rank-one segment shocks populate the non-Gaussian boundary.

This proposal uses a coefficient-level sufficient condition for a product of two balanced slices, not a published condition. It is plausible in large marketplaces when no buyer, seller, or single row or column of pair interactions carries a macroscopic fraction of the design variance; bounded diffuse additive effects and bounded-degree or delocalized segment interactions satisfy the cap after normalization. The derived-influence proposition connects it algebraically to the published single-slice swap influence of Filmus et al.

The equality subclass is nonempty for single-exposure row-additive schedules, including the declared row witness, because the contrast contains only one random exposure component and the Neyman envelope then has no cross-component slack.

standard.name: uniform coverage constraint for minimax expected-measure confidence sets

definitions.name: canonical coefficient projection
definitions.construction: Compute \(A_i=(n^2\kappa_n)^{-1}\sum_{j,\gamma}c_\gamma u_\gamma Y^\gamma_{ij}\), \(B_j=(n^2\kappa_n)^{-1}\sum_{i,\gamma}c_\gamma v_\gamma Y^\gamma_{ij}\), and \(D_{ij}=(n^2\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\sum_\gamma c_\gamma u_\gamma v_\gamma Y^\gamma_{ij}\); then set \(a=P_nA\), \(b=P_nB\), and \(C=P_nDP_n\).

definitions.name: spectrally controlled low-influence MRD schedules
definitions.construction: \(F_n(\rho)=\{Y\in([-2,2]^{n\times n})^\Gamma: Y\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:exposure-consistency},\text{ass:bounded-schedule},\text{ass:variance-floor},\text{ass:spectral-cap},\text{ass:aggregate-low-influence}\}\) for each even \(n\geq4\).

definitions.name: additive envelope-equality subclass
definitions.construction: \(F_n^{=}=\{Y\in F_n(0):Y\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:envelope-equality}\}\) for each even \(n\geq4\).

definitions.name: uniformly honest observed-data interval sequences
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_\alpha(\rho)=\{(I_n)_{n\geq4,\ n\ {\rm even}}: I_n\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:uniform-honesty}\}\).

definitions.name: sharp honest normalized expected-length frontier
definitions.construction: \(R_\alpha(\rho)=\inf_{(I_n)\in\mathcal H_\alpha(\rho)}\limsup_{n\to\infty,\ n\ {\rm even}}\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(I_n)]/M(Y)\).

definitions.name: finite-sample all-observed-policy value
definitions.construction: \(R_{n,\alpha}(\rho)=\inf_{I_n}\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(I_n)]/M(Y)\), where the infimum is over every possibly independently randomized closed interval measurable with respect to \(O_n\) and satisfying \(\inf_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\Pr_Y\{\tau(Y)\in I_n\}\geq1-\alpha\).

definitions.name: shared-coordinate Gaussian analogue
definitions.construction: \(Q_n=a^\top G+b^\top H+G^\top CH\), where \(G\) and \(H\) are independent \(N(0,P_n)\) vectors.

definitions.name: swap-based coordinate influences on the balanced product slice
definitions.construction: For \(i\in B_n\), let \(r^{(ii')}\) swap coordinates \(i\) and \(i'\) of \(r\), and define \(\operatorname{Inf}^{B}_{i}(f_Y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i'=1}^n\mathbb E[(f_Y(r,s)-f_Y(r^{(ii')},s))^2]\). For \(j\in S_n\), define \(\operatorname{Inf}^{S}_{j}(f_Y)=n^{-1}\sum_{j'=1}^n\mathbb E[(f_Y(r,s)-f_Y(r,s^{(jj')}))^2]\).

definitions.name: row-additive nonemptiness witness
definitions.construction: Let \(x_i=1\) for \(i\leq n/2\) and \(x_i=-1\) otherwise; set \((Y^{\mathrm{row}})^{\mathrm{tr}}_{ij}=x_i\) and \((Y^{\mathrm{row}})^\gamma_{ij}=0\) for \(\gamma\neq\mathrm{tr}\).

definitions.name: finite observed-experiment interval game
definitions.construction: \(V_\Theta\) is the optimum of \(\min_{t,\Pi}t\) subject, for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), to \(\sum_xP_\theta(x)\sum_I\Pi(I\mid x)\mathbf 1\{\tau(\theta)\in I\}\geq1-\alpha\), \(\sum_xP_\theta(x)\sum_I\Pi(I\mid x)\operatorname{length}(I)/M(\theta)\leq t\), \(\sum_I\Pi(I\mid x)=1\), and \(\Pi(I\mid x)\geq0\); the action set contains all closed intervals with endpoints in \(\{-8,8\}\cup\{\tau(\theta):\theta\in\Theta\}\).

definitions.name: four-by-four globally compatible completion game
definitions.construction: Fix \(n=4\). For \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), the fixed schedule \(\theta_\varepsilon\) has \(Y^{\mathrm{tr}}_{11}=\varepsilon\) and \(Y^\gamma_{ij}=0\) for every other \((i,j,\gamma)\); set \(\theta_+=\theta_1\), \(\theta_-=\theta_{-1}\), and \(\Theta_{\pm}=\{\theta_+,\theta_-\}\).

definitions.name: observable primal policy for the two-state game
definitions.construction: Under \(\Theta_{\pm}\), if \(W_{B,1}=W_{S,1}=1\), let \(\Pi_{\pm}\) return the singleton \(\{Y^{(W_{B,1},W_{S,1})}_{11}/16\}\). Otherwise, independently return \([-1/16,1/16]\) with probability \(1-8\alpha/3\), \(\{-1/16\}\) with probability \(4\alpha/3\), and \(\{1/16\}\) with probability \(4\alpha/3\).

definitions.name: public randomized outcome and observation quantizer
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal G_\eta=\{-2+k\eta:0\leq k\leq4/\eta\}\) and \(Q_\eta(y,d)=\max\{-2,\min\{2,-2+\eta\lfloor(y+2)/\eta+d\rfloor\}\}\). For \(O_n=(w_B,w_S,z)\), set \(\mathsf q_\eta(O_n,D_n)=(w_B,w_S,(Q_\eta(z_{ij},D_{ij}))_{ij})\), using public independent dither \(D_n\).

definitions.name: row--column relabeling orbit cells
definitions.construction: The group \(\mathfrak R_n=\mathfrak S_n\times\mathfrak S_n\) acts by \((\pi,\sigma)\cdot(w_B,w_S,z)=(w_B\circ\pi^{-1},w_S\circ\sigma^{-1},(z_{\pi^{-1}(i),\sigma^{-1}(j)})_{ij})\). Define \(x\sim_{n,\eta}x'\) exactly when \(x'=g\cdot x\) for some \(g\in\mathfrak R_n\), and choose the lexicographically least labeled triple as the canonical representative of each orbit.

definitions.name: finite robust globally compatible completion cells
definitions.construction: For each \(q=(q^\gamma_{ij})\in(\mathcal G_\eta^{n\times n})^\Gamma\), define the genuine-schedule cell \(\mathcal B(q)=\{Y\in F_n(\rho):|Y^\gamma_{ij}-q^\gamma_{ij}|\leq\eta\text{ for every }i,j,\gamma\}\). Put \(d_{n,\eta}=\eta n^{-2}\). Retain exactly the \(q\) for which \(\mathcal B(q)\neq\varnothing\), and store \(t=(q,\tau_-(q),\tau_+(q),m_-(q),m_+(q),C_K(q))\), where \(\tau_-(q)=d_{n,\eta}\lfloor d_{n,\eta}^{-1}\inf_{Y\in\mathcal B(q)}\tau(Y)\rfloor\), \(\tau_+(q)=d_{n,\eta}\lceil d_{n,\eta}^{-1}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal B(q)}\tau(Y)\rceil\), and \(m_-(q),m_+(q)\) are the corresponding outward rational bounds for \(\inf_{Y\in\mathcal B(q)}M(Y)\) and \(\sup_{Y\in\mathcal B(q)}M(Y)\). The symbol \(q\) is only a cell label and is never used as a schedule. The object \(C_K(q)\) is an outward interval enclosure, common to all \(Y\in\mathcal B(q)\), of the first \(K\) ordered singular triples of \(C(Y)\). Membership, extrema, square roots, and spectral enclosures are computed by exact real-algebraic quantifier elimination and outward rational refinement. The variance floor gives \(m_-(q)>0\), and the stored coordinate bounds certify \(\tau_+(q)-\tau_-(q)\leq8\eta+d_{n,\eta}\) and \(m_+(q)-m_-(q)\leq8\eta+d_{n,\eta}\).

definitions.name: robust observation cells, actions, likelihoods, and losses
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal O^*_{n,K,\eta}\) contain every labeled triple \(o^*=(w_B,w_S,z)\) with balanced \(w_B,w_S\) and \(z\in\mathcal G_\eta^{n\times n}\), and let \(\mathcal X_{n,K,\eta}\) be its finite set of canonical \(\sim_{n,\eta}\)-orbits. Let \(\mathcal A_{n,K,\eta}=\{[l,u]:l,u\in\eta n^{-2}\mathbb Z\cap[-8,8],\ l\leq u\}\). For every retained cell \(q\), every genuine completion \(Y\in\mathcal B(q)\), and every orbit \(x\), define \(p_Y(x)=\binom n{n/2}^{-2}\sum_{w_B,w_S}\Pr_{D_n}\{[\mathsf q_\eta(O_n(Y,w_B,w_S),D_n)]_{\sim_{n,\eta}}=x\}\). Each scalar dither probability is exactly \(1-r\) or \(r\), where \(r=(Y^\gamma_{ij}+2)/\eta-\lfloor(Y^\gamma_{ij}+2)/\eta\rfloor\), with the declared clipping at the endpoints, so \(p_Y(x)\) is a displayed piecewise-polynomial function of the actual schedule. The genuine-experiment entries are \(g_Y(x,A)=\mathbf1\{\tau(Y)\in A\}\) and \(\ell_Y(x,A)=\operatorname{length}(A)/M(Y)\).

definitions.name: robust restriction and orbit-lifting kernels
definitions.construction: For an actual observation \(o\), set \(K_\downarrow(x\mid o)=\Pr_{D_n}\{[\mathsf q_\eta(o,D_n)]_{\sim_{n,\eta}}=x\}\). For each orbit \(x\), let \(K_\uparrow(\cdot\mid x)\) be uniform on the finitely many labeled grid observations \(o^*\in\mathcal O^*_{n,K,\eta}\) whose orbit is \(x\). For a full-observation rule \(\delta\), \(\delta^\downarrow\) draws \(o^*\sim K_\uparrow(\cdot\mid x)\), applies \(\delta\) to \(o^*\), rounds both endpoints outward to \(\eta n^{-2}\mathbb Z\), and clips to \([-8,8]\). For a finite rule \(\pi\), \(\pi^\uparrow\) draws \(x\sim K_\downarrow(\cdot\mid o)\), draws \([l,u]\sim\pi(\cdot\mid x)\), and returns \([\max\{-8,l-4\eta\},\min\{8,u+4\eta\}]\). For \(d_Y^{\mathrm{cov}}(A)=\mathbf1\{\tau(Y)\in A\}\) and \(d_Y^{\mathrm{len}}(A)=\operatorname{length}(A)/M(Y)\), let \(\phi\) assign an action separately to each element of the finite disjoint union \(\mathcal Z_n\sqcup\mathcal O^*_{n,K,\eta}\). Define \(\Delta^d_{Y,\phi}=|\binom n{n/2}^{-2}\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}d_Y^d(\phi(z))-\binom n{n/2}^{-2}\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}\sum_xK_\downarrow(x\mid O_n(Y,z))\sum_{o^*}K_\uparrow(o^*\mid x)d_Y^d(\phi(o^*))|\). Then \(\chi_{n,K,\eta}=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_{n,K,\eta}(\rho)}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal B(q)}\max_{\phi\in\mathcal A_{n,K,\eta}^{\,\mathcal Z_n\sqcup\mathcal O^*_{n,K,\eta}}}\max_{d\in\{\mathrm{cov},\mathrm{len}\}}\Delta^d_{Y,\phi}\). The selector maximum is finite, and the remaining compact semialgebraic supremum is returned as an outward rational certificate by quantifier elimination.

definitions.name: all-policy row--column symmetrization
definitions.construction: For every randomized labeled-grid rule \(\delta\), define \(\operatorname{Sym}_{n,\eta}\delta(A\mid o^*)=|\mathfrak R_n|^{-1}\sum_{g\in\mathfrak R_n}\delta(A\mid g\cdot o^*)\). This kernel is constant on each orbit, so \(\delta^{\mathrm{orb}}(A\mid[o^*])=\operatorname{Sym}_{n,\eta}\delta(A\mid o^*)\) defines a unique rule on \(\mathcal X_{n,K,\eta}\). For an arbitrary measurable full-observation rule, evaluate it at the finitely many labeled grid tables, round its endpoints outward to \(\eta n^{-2}\mathbb Z\cap[-8,8]\), and apply the same finite group average; equivalently, draw a labeled representative with \(K_\uparrow\) and then apply the rounded rule. Thus the construction applies to every measurable interval rule after public quantization, without a continuity or equivariance restriction.

definitions.name: formal robust completion-game input
definitions.construction: The game \(\mathsf{Game}_{K,\eta}(\alpha,\rho)\) chooses \(t\) and a Markov policy \(\pi(A\mid x)\) on the finite sets \(\mathcal X_{n,K,\eta}\) and \(\mathcal A_{n,K,\eta}\). For every retained \(q\) and every genuine schedule \(Y\in\mathcal B(q)\), it imposes \(\sum_xp_Y(x)\sum_A\pi(A\mid x)\mathbf1\{\tau(Y)\in A\}\geq1-\alpha\) and \(\sum_xp_Y(x)\sum_A\pi(A\mid x)\operatorname{length}(A)/M(Y)\leq t\), together with the simplex constraints on \(\pi\). Its value is \(v_{K,\eta}(\alpha,\rho)\). This is a finite-dimensional robust semialgebraic program: all actions and observation coordinates are finite, and its universal completion constraints are exactly decidable to prescribed outward rational error. A certificate consists of an interval policy, finitely many active genuine completions \(Y\in\mathcal B(q)\) with dual weights, a value enclosure, the two kernels, and the outward bound for \(\chi_{n,K,\eta}\).

definitions.name: additive globally compatible completion benchmark
definitions.construction: For each even \(n\geq4\) and \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), define the fixed schedule \((Y_{n,\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{add}})^\gamma_{ij}=L_0p_i+\varepsilon d_0\mathbf1\{i=1,\gamma=\mathrm{tr}\}\) for every \(i,j,\gamma\). Set \(\theta_{n,+}^{\mathrm{add}}=Y_{n,1}^{\mathrm{add}}\), \(\theta_{n,-}^{\mathrm{add}}=Y_{n,-1}^{\mathrm{add}}\), and \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm{add}}=\{\theta_{n,+}^{\mathrm{add}},\theta_{n,-}^{\mathrm{add}}\}\). The common row component supplies diffuse envelope variation but cancels from the direct-effect contrast, and the sign ambiguity is a row-additive treatment potential outcome.

definitions.name: persistent-rank globally compatible completion family
definitions.construction: For each even \(n\geq4\) and \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), define one fixed schedule by \((Y_{n,\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{int}})^\gamma_{ij}=L_0p_ip_j+\varepsilon d_0\mathbf1\{i=j=1,\gamma=\mathrm{tr}\}\) for every \(i,j,\gamma\). Set \(\theta_{n,+}^{\mathrm{int}}=Y_{n,1}^{\mathrm{int}}\), \(\theta_{n,-}^{\mathrm{int}}=Y_{n,-1}^{\mathrm{int}}\), and \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm{int}}=\{\theta_{n,+}^{\mathrm{int}},\theta_{n,-}^{\mathrm{int}}\}\). The common term is a declared rank-one interaction, while the sign ambiguity is confined to the treatment potential outcome at \((1,1)\).

definitions.name: parameterized cancelled two-exposure orbit
definitions.construction: For every even \(n\geq4\) and \(\vartheta\in[-1,1]\), define \((Y_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{can}})^{\mathrm{tr}}_{ij}=\vartheta+L_0p_i\), \((Y_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{can}})^{\mathrm{ib}}_{ij}=L_0p_i\), and \((Y_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{can}})^{\mathrm{is}}_{ij}=(Y_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{can}})^{\mathrm{cc}}_{ij}=0\) for all \(i,j\). Let \(F_n^{\mathrm{can}}=\{g\cdot Y_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{can}}:g\in\mathfrak R_n,\ \vartheta\in[-1,1]\}\), where relabeling acts simultaneously on all four potential-outcome matrices. The comparison policy is the observable singleton \(I_n^{\mathrm{can}}(O_n)=\{\widehat\tau\}\).

statements.statement: For every fixed schedule \(Y\), the canonical projection is unique and \(\widehat\tau-\tau(Y)=a^\top r+b^\top s+r^\top Cs\), with \(\mathbf 1_n^\top a=\mathbf 1_n^\top b=0\) and \(P_nCP_n=C\).
statements.justification: The exact decomposition fixes the common coordinate system in which additive nuisance and interaction alignment can be compared.
statements.gap: MasoeroEtAl2026MRD decomposes exposure-mean variances, while SudijonoEtAl2026Regression analyzes related double-randomization projections; neither states this unique contrast-level shared-coordinate form for the full four-schedule direct-effect contrast.
statements.consumer: The decomposition supplies the state variables for a nonnormal calibration of the published SMRD contrast.

statements.justification: The identity separates actual randomization variance from the unobservable Neyman normalization used in the decision loss.
statements.gap: MasoeroEtAl2026MRD gives exact exposure-component variances and the equation \(41\) envelope; the proposition records the contrast-level linear--bilinear variance geometry required by the frontier.
statements.consumer: The normalization makes interval policies comparable across Comola--Prina-type schedules with different additive and interactive composition.

statements.statement: For every \(Y\in F_n(\rho)\), the swap-based influences of the normalized polynomial satisfy \(\operatorname{Inf}^{B}_{i}(f_Y)=2M(Y)^{-2}\{a_i^2+\|C_{i\cdot}\|_2^2+n^{-1}(\|a\|_2^2+\|C\|_F^2)\}\) and \(\operatorname{Inf}^{S}_{j}(f_Y)=2M(Y)^{-2}\{b_j^2+\|C_{\cdot j}\|_2^2+n^{-1}(\|b\|_2^2+\|C\|_F^2)\}\). Hence \(\max_i\operatorname{Inf}^{B}_{i}(f_Y)\vee\max_j\operatorname{Inf}^{S}_{j}(f_Y)\leq4n^{-1/4}+2n^{-1}\).
statements.justification: Filmus et al. define coordinate influence by averaging squared swap differences. Here centering gives the displayed identities exactly; the declared \(n^{-1/8}\) coefficient cap is squared by that definition, so both product-slice influence arrays are \(O(n^{-1/4})\), and the sixth-root influence term used in the sequential degree-two replacement is \(O(n^{-1/24})\).
statements.gap: FilmusKindlerMosselWimmer2018Slice, Section 2.1 and Theorem 5.8, treats one harmonic slice polynomial through swap influences; it does not derive the two influence arrays for an aligned rectangular linear--bilinear MRD contrast.
statements.consumer: The identities let a referee check directly that the schedule-level normalization is sufficient for both buyer and seller replacement steps.

statements.statement: For every \(Y\in F_n(0)\), \(C=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_Y(\widehat\tau)=\|a\|_2^2+\|b\|_2^2\leq V^+(Y)\). Equality is asserted only for \(Y\in F_n^{=}\); on that subclass \(Q_n/M(Y)\sim N(0,1)\), so the oracle Gaussian location interval with half-width \(z_{1-\alpha/2}M(Y)\) has normalized length \(2z_{1-\alpha/2}\).
statements.justification: This separates the general additive inequality from the special no-envelope-slack reduction needed to recover the standard Gaussian benchmark.
statements.gap: Equation \(41\) of MasoeroEtAl2026MRD is a variance upper envelope and need not equal the variance of a contrast; the equality subclass records exactly when the familiar Gaussian constant is a valid sanity check.
statements.consumer: The reduction prevents the sharp-frontier calculation from being benchmarked against an oracle constant on schedules where the Neyman envelope is slack.

statements.statement: There is an explicit even integer \(n_0\) such that \(Y^{\mathrm{row}}\in F_n^{=}\subseteq F_n(\rho)\) for every even \(n\geq n_0\) and every \(\rho\in[0,1]\); hence both the envelope-equality subclass and the asymptotic suprema defining \(R_\alpha(\rho)\) are eventually nonempty.
statements.justification: Nonemptiness prevents a vacuous asymptotic decision problem at small or large spectral radius.
statements.gap: The published MRD asymptotics do not define the present triangular classes or verify that the joint variance-floor and influence restrictions can be met uniformly in \(\rho\).
statements.consumer: The construction provides a valid benchmark subexperiment for every point on the frontier curve.

statements.statement: Let \(X_{n,Y}=(\widehat\tau-\tau(Y))/M(Y)\) and \(Z_{n,Y}=Q_n/M(Y)\). Uniformly over \(Y\in F_n(\rho)\), \(W_1(\mathcal L_Y(X_{n,Y}),\mathcal L_Y(Z_{n,Y}))\leq\delta_n\). For every \(h\in(0,1)\) and every fixed or independently randomized closed interval \(J\subseteq\mathbb R\), \(\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}|\Pr_Y\{X_{n,Y}\in J\}-\Pr_Y\{Z_{n,Y}\in J\}|\leq\delta_n/h+2\mathfrak a_{n,\rho}(h)\). For every measurable \(\ell:\mathbb R\to[0,T]\), including truncated normalized-length losses, \(\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}|\mathbb E_Y[(\mathcal S_h\ell)(X_{n,Y})]-\mathbb E_Y[(\mathcal S_h\ell)(Z_{n,Y})]|\leq T\delta_n/h\). These bounds preserve the shared Gaussian coordinates in the linear and bilinear terms.
statements.justification: The displayed bandwidth, boundary-mass, and truncation terms make the scalar coverage and smoothed expected-length consequences of the coupling directly checkable while preserving interaction alignment.
statements.gap: FilmusKindlerMosselWimmer2018Slice treats low-degree functions on one slice, NourdinPeccatiReinert2010Universality treats homogeneous sums, and SudijonoEtAl2026Regression gives a normal bound; none supplies this product-slice aligned-chaos and nonsmooth-risk statement.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies certified calibration errors for interval rules whose discontinuities are smoothed or whose Gaussian-chaos boundary mass is explicitly evaluated.

statements.statement: Every sequence \(Y_n\in F_n(\rho)\) has a subsequence along which \(Q_n/M(Y_n)\) converges to \(\sigma_0Z_0+\sum_{k\geq1}(\xi_k\beta_k+\zeta_k\gamma_k+\lambda_k\xi_k\zeta_k)\), where the coefficient sequences arise as the aligned singular-value and linear-projection limits, belong to \(\ell_2\), and satisfy \(\sigma_0^2+\sum_{k\geq1}(\beta_k^2+\gamma_k^2+\lambda_k^2)\leq1\). Such a subsequential limit is Gaussian if and only if \(\|C\|_{\mathrm{op}}/M\to0\) along that subsequence.
statements.justification: The boundary identifies the nuisance coordinates that a sharp interval game must retain and gives an exact normality frontier.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaEtAl2024QuadraticChaos, Theorem \(1.4\), treats symmetric quadratic forms, while SudijonoEtAl2026Regression, arXiv:2603.19480v2, Section \(5.1\), displays the rank-one factorization and its product-normal limit; neither gives the rectangular aligned linear-plus-bilinear converse and realizability result for balanced MRD schedules.
statements.consumer: The result tells marketplace analysts when Gaussian calibration is valid and when finite-rank product-normal components must be retained.

statements.statement: For every finite globally compatible schedule family \(\Theta\), \(V_\Theta\) equals the minimax worst-case normalized expected length over randomized closed-interval rules with coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) on \(\Theta\). Its linear-program dual is attained by a finite mixture over schedule-specific coverage and risk constraints, and rational input probabilities admit a rational primal--dual certificate computable to additive error \(\eta\) in time polynomial in the explicit game-table size, its bit length, and \(\log(1/\eta)\).
statements.justification: A common primal--dual object makes the upper interval and the all-rule lower certificate auditable in the same finite experiment.
statements.gap: EvansHansenStark2005MES proves expected-measure Bayes--minimax duality and BryanMcMahanSchaferSchneider2007MES studies finite confidence-region games; the proposition specializes these ingredients to randomized interval actions with schedule-specific MRD normalization.
statements.consumer: The certificate is the computational primitive used to audit every finite calibration step of the frontier algorithm.

statements.statement: For every \(\rho\in[1/\sqrt{3},1]\), \(\theta_+,\theta_-\in F_4(\rho)\), with \(\tau(\theta_\pm)=\pm1/16\), \(M(\theta_\pm)=\sqrt{3}/16\), and \(\|C(\theta_\pm)\|_{\mathrm{op}}/M(\theta_\pm)=1/\sqrt{3}\). The observation reveals the sign exactly when \(W_{B,1}=W_{S,1}=1\), an event of probability \(1/4\); on its complement, of probability \(3/4\), both schedules generate the same zero outcome table. The observable rule \(\Pi_{\pm}\) has coverage exactly \(1-\alpha\) under both schedules and worst-case normalized expected length \(V_{\pm}=(3/2-4\alpha)/\sqrt{3}\), which is the exact game value. After eliminating the zero-length revealing actions and quotienting the common observation orbit, a dual certificate puts probability \(1/2\) on each schedule, uses coverage multiplier \(2/\sqrt{3}\) for each schedule, and uses common-orbit normalization multiplier \(\sqrt{3}/2\); its value equals the primal value.
statements.justification: This closed-form game audits global schedule compatibility, observable randomization, and the matching lower certificate before those ingredients are scaled to the frontier approximation.
statements.gap: The binary completion games of RigdonHudgens2015Binary and the partial-interference inversion of RigdonHudgens2015Interference do not contain this crossed continuous-outcome two-schedule game or its normalized expected-length dual value.
statements.consumer: The game is a unit test for the finite completion-game generator and its primal--dual certificate output.

statements.statement: For every even \(n\), every randomized labeled-grid interval kernel \(\delta\), every schedule \(Y\in F_n(\rho)\), and \(d\in\{\mathrm{cov},\mathrm{len}\}\), let \(L_Y^{\mathrm{cov}}(A)=\mathbf1\{\tau(Y)\in A\}\) and \(L_Y^{\mathrm{len}}(A)=\operatorname{length}(A)/M(Y)\). Then \(F_n(\rho)\) is closed under \(\mathfrak R_n\), \(\tau(g\cdot Y)=\tau(Y)\), \(M(g\cdot Y)=M(Y)\), and design-and-dither equivariance gives the exact identity \[\mathbb E_{Y,D_n}\!\left[\int L_Y^d(A)\,\operatorname{Sym}_{n,\eta}\delta\{dA\mid\mathsf q_\eta(O_n,D_n)\}\right]=|\mathfrak R_n|^{-1}\sum_{g\in\mathfrak R_n}\mathbb E_{g\cdot Y,D_n}\!\left[\int L_{g\cdot Y}^d(A)\,\delta\{dA\mid\mathsf q_\eta(O_n,D_n)\}\right].\] Consequently symmetrization weakly increases worst-schedule coverage and weakly decreases worst-schedule normalized expected length. The symmetrized kernel factors uniquely through \(\mathcal X_{n,K,\eta}\). For every arbitrary measurable full-observation rule \(I_n\), including randomized rules, public quantization followed by \(K_\uparrow\) produces exactly the orbit average of its outward-rounded evaluations on the finite labeled grid; hence no measurable policy is lost before the separately quantified rounding and dither residuals. This identity is the first obligation in the finite-game certificate.
statements.justification: The exact group-average identity, rather than an informal appeal to symmetry, is what permits a lower bound against every measurable observed-data interval after quantization.
statements.gap: EvansHansenStark2005MES and BryanMcMahanSchaferSchneider2007MES optimize finite confidence rules, but neither proves an all-measurable-policy quotient for a relabeling-closed deterministic MRD experiment with public randomized quantization.
statements.consumer: The lemma is the first D0 check for replacing the full labeled-table policy space by the finite orbit policy space without weakening the minimax lower bound.

statements.statement: For every even \(n\geq4\), \(1\leq K\leq n-1\), \(\eta^{-1}\in\mathbb N\) with \(\eta\leq1/8\), and \(0<q<\alpha\), establish the following inequalities using only the robust objects declared above. For every clipped randomized \(O_n\)-measurable rule \(\delta\), its restricted rule obeys \(\inf_{q_0\in\mathcal Q_{n,K,\eta}(\rho)}\inf_{Y\in\mathcal B(q_0)}\Pr_Y\{\tau(Y)\in\delta^\downarrow\}\geq\inf_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\Pr_Y\{\tau(Y)\in\delta\}-\chi_{n,K,\eta}\) and \(\sup_{q_0\in\mathcal Q_{n,K,\eta}(\rho)}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal B(q_0)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(\delta^\downarrow)]/M(Y)\leq\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(\delta)]/M(Y)+80n\eta+\chi_{n,K,\eta}\). For every finite-game rule \(\pi\), its expanded lift obeys \(\inf_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\Pr_Y\{\tau(Y)\in\pi^\uparrow\}\geq\inf_{q_0\in\mathcal Q_{n,K,\eta}(\rho)}\inf_{Y\in\mathcal B(q_0)}\Pr_Y\{\tau(Y)\in\pi\}\) and \(\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(\pi^\uparrow)]/M(Y)\leq\sup_{q_0\in\mathcal Q_{n,K,\eta}(\rho)}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal B(q_0)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(\pi)]/M(Y)+80n\eta\). Prove that replacing the spectral tail beyond rank \(K\) changes each truncated calibrated risk by at most \(3/(2\sqrt{K+1})\), verify the displayed semialgebraic maximum defining \(\chi_{n,K,\eta}\), and derive \(v_{K,\eta}(\alpha+q,\rho)-e_{n,K,\eta,q}\leq R_{n,\alpha}(\rho)\leq v_{K,\eta}(\alpha-q,\rho)+e_{n,K,\eta,q}\). The handle is row--column orbit symmetrization followed by a risk-specific Le Cam comparison using public dither and endpoint expansion. The required terminating certificate is \(\chi_{n,K_n,\eta_n}\leq\eta_n\) for \(K_n=n-1\), \(\eta_n=n^{-3}\), and \(q_n=n^{-1/4}\).
statements.justification: After the exact all-policy orbit identity, the robust quantifiers make each row a family of genuine fixed-schedule experiments and isolate the remaining dither, rounding, rank, and coverage-slack errors without substituting a grid center for a schedule.
statements.gap: Finite confidence-set games and scalar slice replacement do not give a risk-specific restriction--lifting comparison for a continuum of deterministic MRD observation laws; the robust completion-cell deficiency is the unresolved certificate.
statements.consumer: A solution supplies a terminating upper policy and a finite active-completion dual certificate for the complete observed-table experiment.

statements.statement: The unadjusted specialization \(I_n^{\mathrm{MRD}}\) of equation \(43\) in Sudijono et al., arXiv:2603.19480v2, and the max-standard-error interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{TW}}\) obtained from equation \(2\) in Davezies, D'Haultfoeuille, and Guyonvarch, arXiv:2506.20749v2, are closed intervals measurable with respect to \(O_n\), so they are observable candidate actions for \(R_{n,\alpha}(\rho)\). Masoero et al.'s camera-ready Theorem \(4.4\), pages \(14\)--\(15\), gives an unbiased estimator of each exposure-mean variance; conservativeness applies only to the assembled contrast envelope obtained by Young's inequality in Theorem \(4.5\), which underlies equations \(41\)--\(43\) of Sudijono et al. Sudijono et al.'s Theorem \(3.2\) proves coverage under Assumptions \(1\)--\(5\), with equation \(47\) and Theorem \(3.4\) governing the vanilla MRD normality and variance consistency; Masoero et al.'s Theorems \(4.7\)--\(4.8\), pages \(15\)--\(17\), impose their own nondegeneracy and normal-approximation conditions. For the two-way interval, Assumption \(1\) requires a dissociated separately exchangeable array with finite second moment and positive marginal variance, Assumption \(2\) requires both cluster counts to diverge, Theorem \(1\) gives pointwise validity, and Theorem \(2\) gives validity uniformly on the displayed classes \(\mathcal P_{m,\mathcal H}\). Outside a subclass on which coverage can be verified directly, each rule is a feasible competitor only when its own cited assumptions hold; those source results do not establish uniform design-based honesty over all fixed schedules in \(F_n(\rho)\). Neither source optimizes worst-case normalized expected length over all \(O_n\)-measurable intervals or gives a same-experiment lower bound, so neither determines \(R_\alpha(\rho)\).
statements.justification: Exact version and theorem locators separate admissibility of the published formulas from the domains on which their coverage results are proved.
statements.gap: The cited procedures are conservative competitors under their stated regimes, not solutions of the all-policy fixed-schedule expected-length game.
statements.consumer: Applied MRD analysts obtain two reproducible benchmark lengths without mistaking either benchmark for the sharp decision value.

statements.statement: For every even \(n\geq4\), \(F_n^{\mathrm{can}}\subset F_n(0)\). If \(Y=g\cdot Y_{n,\vartheta}^{\mathrm{can}}\) with buyer permutation \(\pi\), write \(p_i^g=p_{\pi^{-1}(i)}\). Then \(\tau(Y)=\widehat\tau=\vartheta\) for every balanced assignment, \(a=b=0\), \(C=0\), and \(M(Y)=2L_0/\sqrt{n-1}\). Hence the data-measurable rule \(I_n^{\mathrm{can}}=\{\widehat\tau\}\) estimates the unknown \(\vartheta\in[-1,1]\) with exact design coverage one and expected length zero. Both \(I_n^{\mathrm{MRD}}\) and \(I_n^{\mathrm{TW}}\) are centered at \(\widehat\tau=\vartheta\) with nonnegative observable half-widths, so on this subclass they also have exact design coverage one under only ass:buyer-half-sampling, ass:seller-half-sampling, ass:assignment-independence, and \(0<\alpha<1/4\). There is a positive-probability balanced assignment event on which the selected buyer half contains both a zero and a nonzero loading and \(\sum_iW_{B,i}p_i^g\neq0\); on this event the two exposure-component sample variances entering the assembled MRD envelope and a one-way component of the two-way max-standard error are strictly positive. Therefore, for every \(Y\in F_n^{\mathrm{can}}\), \[0=\frac{\mathbb E_Y\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{can}})}{M(Y)}<\min\!\left\{\frac{\mathbb E_Y\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{MRD}})}{M(Y)},\frac{\mathbb E_Y\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{TW}})}{M(Y)}\right\}.\] Their broader published coverage claims still require, respectively, Sudijono et al.'s Assumptions \(1\)--\(5\) and Theorems \(3.2\)--\(3.4\), and Davezies et al.'s Assumptions \(1\)--\(2\) and Theorems \(1\)--\(2\).
statements.justification: The parameterized cancellation orbit has an unknown direct-effect level and nonconstant potential outcomes, yet its row nuisance cancels observably; the exact singleton is strictly shorter than both published analytic rules.
statements.gap: SudijonoEtAl2026Regression and DaveziesDHaultfoeuilleGuyonvarch2026TwoWay establish validity of designated intervals under their own asymptotic regimes, but neither identifies a parameterized fixed-schedule subclass on which an observable exact interval strictly dominates its expected length.
statements.consumer: The subclass supplies a falsifiable benchmark for software implementing the frontier policy and quantifies the cost of ignoring exact cross-exposure cancellation in marketplace tables.

statements.statement: For every even \(n\geq4\), all schedules in \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm{add}}\cup\Theta_n^{\mathrm{int}}\) are bounded and globally compatible, and for every sufficiently large even \(n\), \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm{add}}\subset F_n(0)\) and \(\Theta_n^{\mathrm{int}}\subset F_n(1)\). The additive states satisfy \(C=0\), \(\tau(\theta_{n,\pm}^{\mathrm{add}})=\pm d_0/n\), and \(M(\theta_{n,\pm}^{\mathrm{add}})=M_n^{\mathrm{add}}\). Their observation laws reveal the sign precisely on \(\{W_{B,1}=1\}\), of probability \(1/2\), so their exact two-state value is \(V_n^{\mathrm{add}}=(1-4\alpha)d_0/(nM_n^{\mathrm{add}})\). The persistent-rank states satisfy \(\tau(\theta_{n,\pm}^{\mathrm{int}})=\pm d_0/n^2\), \(M(\theta_{n,\pm}^{\mathrm{int}})=M_n^\star\), and \(\|C(\theta_{n,\pm}^{\mathrm{int}})\|_{\mathrm{op}}/M_n^\star=\rho_n^\star\to1\). Their observation laws reveal the sign precisely on \(\{W_{B,1}=W_{S,1}=1\}\), of probability \(1/4\), so their exact value is \(V_n^{\mathrm{int}}=(3/2-4\alpha)d_0/(n^2M_n^\star)\). Moreover, \(V_n^{\mathrm{int}}/V_n^{\mathrm{add}}\to0\); hence the persistent-rank and additive admissible completion games have strictly different normalized decision values for every sufficiently large even \(n\).
statements.justification: The explicit calculation shows that interaction rank is decision-relevant for normalized completion games, rather than merely a possible change in a statistic's limit law.
statements.gap: Section \(5.1\) of Sudijono et al. gives a rank-one product-normal limit but does not compute an observed-experiment confidence-game value or compare it with an additive completion game.
statements.consumer: The separation prevents the frontier algorithm from discarding persistent singular directions and using additive completion games as universal lower certificates.

statements.statement: Using the formal finite completion table with \(K_n=n-1\), \(\eta_n=n^{-3}\), \(q_n=n^{-1/4}\), and a certified \(\chi_{n,K_n,\eta_n}\leq\eta_n\), determine the limit characterization of \(R_\alpha(\rho)\) for every \(\rho\in[0,1]\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), construct from \(O_n\) and independent randomization a sequence \((I_n^\varepsilon)\in\mathcal H_\alpha(\rho)\), defined for every even \(n\geq4\), such that \(\limsup_{n\to\infty,\ n\ {\rm even}}\sup_{Y\in F_n(\rho)}\mathbb E_Y[\operatorname{length}(I_n^\varepsilon)]/M(Y)\leq R_\alpha(\rho)+\varepsilon\). The finite-game construction must apply for every sufficiently large even \(n\); on the finitely many smaller even sizes use the observable interval \([-8,8]\). Prove the matching lower bound against every \((I_n)\in\mathcal H_\alpha(\rho)\) on the same complete observation experiment. The finite algorithm must return interval endpoints, a dual mixture supported on genuine globally compatible completions from the robust cells, the numerical value, and the displayed rational error certificate, and it must determine whether the curve is flat or changes when finite-rank interactions persist.
statements.justification: This is the sharp decision-theoretic kernel: it jointly demands an observable attaining policy and a same-observation-experiment lower bound, rather than an oracle calibration or a statistic-level approximation.
statements.gap: MasoeroEtAl2026MRD and DaveziesDHaultfoeuilleGuyonvarch2026TwoWay provide conservative inference, while EvansHansenStark2005MES, RigdonHudgens2015Binary, RigdonHudgens2015Interference, and AronowChangLopatto2025FastExactCI supply decision or completion ingredients in simpler experiments; no source determines the all-policy four-exposure MRD expected-length value or supplies a convergent certified algorithm for it.
statements.consumer: A solution gives an operational sharp benchmark for published marketplace MRD inference and a principled interval for the Liu--Shaikh--Toulis reanalysis of the Comola--Prina savings-network experiment.

sampling_model.design: Two independent balanced complete randomizations, one on \(n\) buyers and one on \(n\) sellers.
sampling_model.units: The \(n^2\) buyer--seller pairs have fixed four-exposure potential outcomes; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(n/2\) buyers and \(n/2\) sellers are selected, producing four observed exposure blocks.
sampling_model.overlap: Every exposure has known design probability \(1/4\) for each pair.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The rule observes \(O_n\) only; the full schedules, \(V^+(Y)\), interaction spectrum, and cross-world covariances are not inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Camera-ready Theorem \(4.4\) gives an unbiased estimator of each exposure-mean variance; Theorem \(4.5\) applies Young's inequality to assemble those estimates into a conservative contrast-variance envelope, while Theorems \(4.7\)--\(4.8\) give consistency and Gaussian approximation under the paper's stated conditions.
In arXiv v2, equation \(43\) and Theorem \(3.2\) give conservative adjusted inference, while Section \(5.1\) records a rank-one product-normal limit as an open uniform-inference direction.
Coverage-constrained expected-measure confidence sets admit a Bayes--minimax test-inversion duality in restricted location families.

For a completely randomized experiment with binary outcomes and no interference, exact finite-population confidence sets are built either from Bonferroni prediction sets for attributable effects or by inversion of permutation tests over observed-data-compatible missing binary potential outcomes.

Under partial and stratified interference in a two-stage randomized experiment with binary outcomes, compatible four-vector potential-outcome schedules are bounded and exact confidence sets for direct, indirect, total, and overall effects are obtained by permutation-test inversion.
Finite minimax expected-size confidence-region problems can be represented and approximated as sparse zero-sum games.
Unidentified one-population potential-outcome covariance has sharp extremal-coupling bounds, yielding asymptotically shortest Wald-type conservative intervals.

Journal of Econometrics 251, Theorem \(4.1\) and Algorithm \(4.3\), compute balanced binary-outcome exact intervals with \(O(n\log n)\) permutation tests; Proposition \(5.3\) controls the Monte Carlo version.
Low-degree low-influence harmonic functions have close laws on a fixed-weight slice and in Gaussian space.
Low-influence homogeneous sums obey quantitative invariance bounds and Gaussian-chaos universality criteria.
Multivariate hypergeometric experiments are asymptotically equivalent to Gaussian experiments under a sparse sampling-fraction regime.
Theorem \(1.4\) characterizes subsequential limits of low-influence symmetric quadratic chaos by Gaussian, Gaussian-mixture, and centered chi-square components.

ArXiv v2 equation \(2\) defines the max-standard-error test and interval, Theorem \(1\) gives pointwise validity, and Theorem \(2\) gives uniform validity on a restricted class of dissociated separately exchangeable laws.
ArXiv v1 Theorem \(2.2\) solves the unrestricted design--estimator minimax mean-squared-error problem for one-population bounded outcomes, and Theorem \(3.1\) gives its second-order expansion.

tldr: Balanced multiple randomization reveals one of four fixed potential outcomes for every buyer--seller pair, leaving the population Neyman scale, cross-world covariance, and interaction alignment latent. The proposal values every interval measurable from the complete observed table. Its finite approximation is a robust game whose first obligation is an exact group-average identity reducing every measurable quantized policy to a row--column orbit rule; each grid row then denotes a cell \(\mathcal B(q)\), while likelihood, coverage, and normalized loss are evaluated for every genuine schedule \(Y\in\mathcal B(q)\). A parameterized cancellation orbit has an unknown direct-effect level that is nevertheless observed exactly and yields strictly shorter expected length than both published analytic competitors, while explicit additive and persistent-rank completion games show that retained spectral directions change finite decision values. The essential target remains the sharp all-observed-policy curve \(R_\alpha(\rho)\), with observable epsilon-attainment and a same-experiment lower bound certified by one finite algorithm.

project_justification.gap: Published MRD theory supplies unbiased exposure-component variance estimators, a conservative assembled contrast envelope, and Gaussian inference under dominance conditions, but it does not value the best honest interval among all functions of the observed four-block table. Existing completion inversion, expected-measure duality, and slice invariance each omit either global four-schedule compatibility, fixed-half product-slice interactions, or all-rule risk transfer.
project_justification.niche: The fixed square-half design isolates an economically relevant decision frontier indexed by the observable-experiment-compatible spectral cap \(\rho\), while retaining latent additive nuisance and unobserved cross-world dependence. This is the smallest benchmark in which persistent interaction chaos and honest adaptation can jointly affect the optimal length constant.
project_justification.fill: An exact policy-symmetrization identity first reduces every measurable randomized quantized rule to the row--column orbit space. Robust completion cells then retain every globally compatible schedule rather than substituting a quantized center, and their common policy is tested against the genuine likelihood, target, and normalization of each cell member; restriction and lifting expose the remaining all-policy discrepancy as \(\chi_{n,K,\eta}\). A parameterized cancellation orbit yields an exact zero-length interval for an unknown direct-effect level and is strictly shorter than both published analytic rules, a persistent-rank subgame proves that the retained spectrum changes a normalized decision value, and the full algorithm must return an observable interval, active-completion dual mixture, value enclosure, and vanishing certificate.

related_work: MasoeroEtAl2026MRD fixes the local-interference SMRD experiment: its camera-ready Assumption \(2.4\) defines exposure consistency, Theorem \(4.4\), pages \(14\)--\(15\), gives an unbiased estimator of each exposure-mean variance, Theorem \(4.5\) assembles the component estimators by Young's inequality into a conservative contrast-variance envelope, Theorem \(4.7\) gives consistency under nondegeneracy, and Theorem \(4.8\), pages \(15\)--\(17\), gives the Gaussian approximation. SudijonoEtAl2026Regression, arXiv:2603.19480v2, equations \(41\)--\(43\) and Theorem \(3.2\), supplies the explicit conservative assembled-envelope interval used as the unadjusted MRD competitor; its Section \(5.1\), equations around the rank-one factorization, gives the product-normal example and explicitly leaves uniform inference across limits open. EvansHansenStark2005MES, Sections \(2.3\) and \(3\), supplies expected-measure Bayes--minimax duality, and BryanMcMahanSchaferSchneider2007MES, Sections \(2\)--\(3\), supplies finite matrix-game computation; neither treats deterministic continuous MRD observation laws or proves the row--column group-average identity for arbitrary measurable policies used here. RigdonHudgens2015Binary, Sections \(2\)--\(3\), inverts compatible missing binary potential outcomes without interference.
